Mecka raises $60 million to expand robotics data and deployment

Sequoia leads the Series B with NVIDIA, M12, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung among the new investors, supporting human-demonstration capture and robot integration.

Mecka ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Funding the data and deployment stack

Mecka announced a $60 million Series B on October 7, led by Sequoia Capital. New investors include NVIDIA, Microsoft’s M12, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung, alongside continued support from Kindred, Framework Ventures and Neo. The funding will expand data infrastructure, the internal research lab and commercial robot deployment.

Recording physical experience

Mecka designs its own multisensor capture hardware and runs recording operations in homes and commercial settings. Its models turn those recordings into motion information, 3D reconstruction and aligned signals. The company focuses on physical experience, including grasping and contact, that robotics teams need to train machines for real tasks.

Integration and financial qualifications

Its integration approach combines hardware, on-site data capture, post-training and ongoing operation. Mecka says it exceeded a $100 million annualized revenue run rate in June and projects $300 million by year-end. These are company-reported figures and forecasts; a run rate is not a full year of recognized revenue. The announcement also does not independently verify robot improvement across every task.
